I'm fairly certain that this is a case where we're really going to want some sort of `typename Args...`, like what is done in `include/sdbusplus/async/client.hpp`.

It is fairly rare to only host exactly 1 interface type (and only want exactly 1 interface type) from a daemon.  Many of our interfaces have some "primary" interface and multiple optional "secondary" interfaces.

If you look at `phosphor-logging` as an example, these are all of the interfaces hosted at any single event entry path:

```
org.freedesktop.DBus.Introspectable
org.freedesktop.DBus.Peer
org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties
xyz.openbmc_project.Association.Definitions
xyz.openbmc_project.Common.FilePath
xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Entry
xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete
xyz.openbmc_project.Software.Version
```

Now, it may be that your particular use case only cares about one of them.  I'm not sure that this is a great API for us to maintain though if it doesn't work for most use-cases.

Yeah, the problem is actually that it will be challenging to universally decode objects since we can't automatically construct a union over the properties for each interface.

I don't think it's just my use case, I suspect that there are lots of cases where you care about a single interface, you know where the object manager is located (by convention or whatever), and so you can do something like:

`proxy.path("/openbmc_xyz/Logging").managed_objects<LoggingEntry>()`

(Similar for sensors, etc.)

And grab the lot of them, without caring about the other kinds coming back. I think that supporting multiple interfaces is going to need a lot more surgery in the message decoding, because it is "context sensitive" (e.g. the variant you are dispatching to depends on the string you decode just before that). If there's a simple solution, I'm open to it 😊

I'm not imaging that this actually replaces the existing code paths, just that in some cases you may try this first, and then fall back to walking the full object tree.

I'm afraid this is more challenging than what you wrote here.  `GetManagedObjects` is hosted by the `org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager`, which is usually created with calls to create a `manager_t`.  The problem is that there is nothing (in either the spec or OpenBMC standards) that dictates what path the ObjectManager.  Some daemons put them at `/`, some put them at `/some/path/of/objects`, and some put in _multiple_ ObjectManagers.

So, in many cases, this call will fail because there is not an ObjectManager there.  In almost every case where you have `/some/path/to/object`, the `ObjectManager` is at least going to be at `/some/path/to` but it could be higher in the hierarchy.  It won't be at `/some/path/to/object` because the `ObjectManager` is required to only give children below the path it is hosted at (ie. it won't give itself).

I'm not actually mandating the path here, is the issue you're describing the fact that the call with fail and throw an exception? (And the user has no way to probe this?) What's the recommended approach for that kind of thing?

(Separately from the discussion about the multiple interfaces.)
